html.body: Date: 2025-02-28 Remarks:Regarding the amendment to the claims:Claims 1-14 are pending in this application, with claims 6-14 currently withdrawn from consideration.This Response is submitted in reply to the Office Action and by this Response, without prejudice and/or disclaimer, claim 5 and the title are amended as requested by the Patent Office in the Office Action, claims 1-4 are cancelled, and new claim 15 is added.No new matter is believed to have been added to this application by this Response. Support for new claim 15 is found in the subject matter of elected claims 1-4; therefore, new claim 15, and its dependent claim 5, are drawn to the elected invention.Regarding the objections to the specification:In Office Action, the Patent Office objects to the title as allegedly being not descriptive and requires a new title that is clearly indicative of the invention to which the claims are directed.In reply, Applicant amends the title to read as follows: "METHODS OF PREPARING/OPTIMIZING PERFUME COMPOSITIONS".In view of the foregoing, reconsideration and withdrawal of the specification objection are respectfully requested.Regarding the claim rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 101:Claims 1-5 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 101 as allegedly being directed to an abstract idea without significantly more. Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection for at least the following reasons.In view of the cancellation of independent claims 1-3, this rejection is moot.Accordingly, reconsideration and withdrawal of this rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 101 are respectfully requested.Regarding the claim rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 112:Claim 5 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as allegedly being indefinite. Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.In view of the amendments to claim 5, this rejection is moot.Accordingly, reconsideration and withdrawal of this rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 112 are respectfully requested.Regarding the claim rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 102:Claims 1-5 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as allegedly being anticipated by WO 2018/206298 to Prigge. Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.In view of the cancellation of independent claims 1-3, this rejection is moot.Accordingly, reconsideration and withdrawal of this rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 102 are respectfully requested.Regarding new independent claim 15:None of the references of record, taken singly or in combination, teaches or suggests the features set forth in newly added claim 15.Thus, the subject matter of newly added claim 15, and its dependent claim, is novel, patentably distinct, and non-obvious in view of the prior art of record, taken singly or in combination.Additionally, Applicant submits claim 15 is not directed to an abstract idea. Instead, the subject matter of claim 15 is more than mere data gathering and is directed to patentable subject matter in accordance with 35 U.S.C. § 101.Further, Applicant submits that the recited features of new claim 15 in the context of the further features of the presently claimed method are tangible steps, which are also novel and unobvious over the prior art. As a result, something 'significantly more' is provided by the presently claimed method.Moreover, the features of new claim 15 patentably integrate the tangible steps of claim 15 into a practical application by reflecting an improvement in other technology or technical field, such as, (i) detecting the perception of difficult to detect perfume performance in relation to well-being and (ii) creating perfume compositions without the necessity of going through many and/or random design iterations of (physical) compositions to arrive at desirable perfume compositions influencing well-being (see page 4, lines 9-14 of the present specification, as originally filed). The features of new claim 15 reduce the number of design iterations needed to arrive at a desirable perfume composition which significantly reduces the time and costs of the creation process of a desirable perfume composition and improves long-term sustainability for desirable perfume composition creation. One important benefit is in the reduction in the discarded organic materials which may in certain instances and jurisdictions be considered VOCs, or difficult to safely dispose of Such a reduction provides a more environmentally responsible process for producing such compositions, as well as a reduction in both time, (actual, and computer resources) and physical materials and energy. Such reductions are tangible improvements over the prior art processes number of design iterations needed to arrive at a desirable perfume composition.Furthermore, claim 15 recites e) selecting a perfume composition with a positive impact on the well-being, f) comparing the perfume ingredients present in those perfume compositions having a positive impact on the well-being, g) identifying odour attributes common to those perfume compositions, and h) creating a new perfume composition with an increased proportion of perfume ingredients with the odour attributes identified in g) which integrate the tangible steps into a practical application by reflecting an improvement to other technology or technical field (i.e., above-mentioned (i) detecting the perception of difficult to detect perfume performance in relation to well-being and (ii) creating perfume compositions without the necessity of going through many design iterations of (physical) compositions to arrive at desirable perfume compositions). Therefore, Applicant submits that these additional features of claim 15, when considered individually and in combination, integrate the tangible steps into a practical application.Accordingly, new claim 15 is patent eligible at least under Prong Two of the Revised Step 2A (see 2019 Revised Patent Subject Matter Eligibility Guidance - Revised Step 2A and also see MPEP 2106.05(b)).Applicant submits that the subject matter of new claim 15 further provides an improved objective, empirical process for the identification of specific perfume ingredients which provide superior benefits to enhancing well-being attributes, and from there providing new perfume compositions, which imparts improved well-being to a human subject.In view of the foregoing, Applicant submits that at least elected claims 5 and 15 are in condition for allowance and requests that the Notice of Allowance for this application be communicated from the Patent Office to the Applicant as soon as possible.Should the Examiner in charge of this application believe that telephonic communication with the undersigned would meaningfully advance the prosecution of this application, the examiner is invited to call the undersigned at their earliest convenience.PETITION FOR ONE-MONTH EXTENSION OF TIMEThe applicant petitions for a one-month extension of time in order to permit for the timely entry of this paper. The Commissioner in order to permit the timely entry of this paper, including any extension of time fees, the Commissioner is authorized to charge any such required fee to Deposit Account No. 14-1263.CONDITIONAL AUTHORIZATION FOR FEESShould any further fee be required by the Commissioner in order to permit the timely entry of this paper, including any extension of time fees, the Commissioner is authorized to charge any such required fee to Deposit Account No. 14-1263.Respectfully submitted, NORRIS MCLAUGHLIN, P.A.Date: February 28, 2025 By /Brian C. Anscomb/ Brian C. Anscomb Attorney for Applicant Reg. No. 48,641 7 Times Square, 21st Floor New York, New York 10036 Phone: (212) 808-0700
